concept.name: dsp_volume_and_clipping_lessons
concept.human_rationale: 1. Cubeb Hardware Volume Failures: On VAIO hardware running PipeWire/pavucontrol, `cubeb_stream_set_volume` often fails silently or returns an error. If the player UI relies solely on OS-level hardware volume (like `cubeb`), users will experience no sound at low slider values or severely restricted volumes. 2. Software Volume Fallback: Always implement a software volume scaling fallback in the `DataCallback` (e.g., `sample * volumeScale`) if the hardware backend reports failure. 3. Psychoacoustic Enhancers vs Hard Clipping: Digital audio floats max out at 1.0f. Hard-clamping (e.g. `out = kCeiling`) shears off the waveform, creating square-wave distortion that physically rattles the laptop chassis. A soft-knee compressor or compander must be used instead to dynamically squash peaks.
concept.execution_logic: Before finalizing any audio DSP integration or volume UI change: - Verify that a `cubeb` set-volume failure is caught and triggers a software-side scaling multiplier. - Run `dsp_preflight_auditor.py` on modified audio C++ files to detect hard-clipping anti-patterns (`if (x > threshold) x = threshold`) and ensure volume parameters are properly passed.
